title: Extraordinary anomaly discipline requires instrument-chain audit, independent controls, versioned provenance, and scope narrowing
summary: A candidate pattern for how extraordinary physical-science anomaly claims move toward knowledge or correction. OPERA, BICEP2, and cold-fusion reevaluation are deliberately different cases: timing-chain failure, foreground/control-model narrowing, and high-rigor replication nonconfirmation. The pattern is about correction discipline, not ridicule. Rev0022 adds GW150914 as a surviving-anomaly positive control and GWOSC/reproducibility audit surfaces so the pattern cannot mature by false-alarm/correction cases alone.

status_history.note: Created in rev0021 after promoting three physical-science anomaly/correction records and two infrastructure rails.
GW150914/GWOSC/Brown/1-OGC controls added; pattern remains candidate-only.

claims.claim: OPERA, BICEP2, and cold-fusion reevaluation support a candidate pattern in which extraordinary anomaly claims require disciplined movement through instrument-chain audit, independent retest/control information, replication or foreground modeling, and explicit status narrowing.
what_would_change_status: A negative-control pass shows the three cases are too heterogeneous for one pattern or should be split into narrower patterns.

claims.claim: arXiv and ADS help make anomaly movement inspectable by preserving versions and indexing literature surfaces, but they do not establish correctness or replace source-level interpretation.
what_would_change_status: A future infrastructure audit changes the role assigned to arXiv or ADS.

claims.claim: This pattern remains candidate-only and explicitly rejects the inference that sincere anomaly claims, failed replications, foreground corrections, and fraud are the same phenomenon.
what_would_change_status: A future red-team pass shows the record still invites shame, overgeneralization, or anti-science framing.

evidence_refs.support_type: candidate status and red-team controls encoded in this record

claims.claim: GW150914 now serves as a positive-control support for MKH-PAT-0017: an extraordinary physical-science signal can survive detector coincidence, statistical testing, open-data release, and later public-data reanalysis rather than resolving as instrument error or foreground/model contamination.
what_would_change_status: Future second-pass review invalidates GW150914 as a positive control, or splits surviving-anomaly controls into another pattern family.

claims.claim: The GWOSC and Brown et al. surfaces refine the anomaly-discipline pattern: open data can make a surviving anomaly more inspectable, while exact workflow reproduction may remain limited by data/provenance differences.
what_would_change_status: A future reproducibility review shows exact workflow reproduction is substantially easier or harder than encoded here.

evidence_profile.why_not_mature: Needs successful anomaly positive controls, fraud/artefact contrast cases, negative controls where extraordinary claims survive, and complete source timelines.

positive_controls_needed: A second surviving-anomaly positive control outside gravitational-wave physics.
A case where versioned provenance and independent retest prevented premature overclaiming before public amplification.
negative_controls_needed: A case with extensive instrumentation where anomaly discipline alone did not settle status because decisive data stayed private, classified, or proprietary.
A case where an extraordinary claim survived initial checks but was later narrowed by theory rather than by instrument/foreground/replication controls.
counterexamples_to_seek: A physical-science anomaly whose correction was mainly theoretical rather than instrumental/foreground/replication driven.
A case where an early anomaly was dismissed too quickly and later revived with stronger evidence.
rollback_triggers: The pattern begins to read as “extraordinary anomalies are probably errors” instead of a discipline/process pattern.
Second-pass review shows one of the three support records is too weak or misclassified.
A better broader pattern absorbs this one, such as denominator visibility or correction-memory infusion.

minimum_next_evidence: one additional positive-control surviving-anomaly case outside GW physics
second-pass primary-source timelines for at least two support records
maturity_gate.do_not_upgrade_before: rev0030 unless controls are promoted earlier and audited

handling_notes: Do not turn physical-science anomaly correction into a shame narrative.
Preserve the value of careful anomaly announcement, independent testing, and claim narrowing.
Do not conflate sincere error, self-correction, and fabrication.

unknowns: No positive-control surviving anomaly has been promoted.
Cold-fusion source depth is still weak relative to OPERA/BICEP2.
No media-amplification or genealogy child records for these anomalies yet.
GW150914 positive-control role has not received second-pass companion-paper review.
No non-gravitational-wave surviving-anomaly control has been promoted yet.
next_actions: Add positive-control surviving anomaly cases, e.g. initially surprising but consolidated discoveries, with careful source selection.
Add contrast records for fraud/fabrication only if the ethics framing is strong.
Second-pass OPERA and BICEP2 full-paper extraction with timeline fields.
Add a second surviving-anomaly control outside gravitational-wave physics.
Add a fraud/fabrication contrast record and a private/proprietary-data negative-control record.
Run a control-coverage matrix review before any pattern-maturity claim.
